question: High levels of estrogen during pregnancy directly lead to which of the following?

options.A: Immediate secretion of mature colostrum from the nipples
options.B: Enlargement of uterine muscle mass and increased blood flow
options.C: Rapid hardening of the bones in the maternal pelvis
options.D: Complete cessation of red blood cell production

explanation: You got it! Estrogen is a growth driver. It helps the uterus stretch, grow bigger, and build up a rich supply of blood vessels for the baby.

question: Why is involving the community during the creation of IEC materials so important?

options.A: It prevents the community from ever asking questions about the disease.
options.B: It builds local ownership and ensures the message fits real community needs.
options.C: It frees the nursing staff from having to participate in health outreaches.
options.D: It guarantees that the health ministry will provide extra funding.

explanation: When people help create the message, they trust it more and are much more likely to follow the health advice.

question: Blood-injection-injury phobias are quite unique. What physical reaction makes them different from other phobias?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of the lower limbs
options.B: Continuous muscle spasms in the face
options.C: An extreme increase in body temperature
options.D: A drop in blood pressure that leads to fainting

explanation: Most phobias send your heart rate racing, but blood and needle phobias often cause a sudden drop in blood pressure and heart rate, leading to good old fainting!

question: A nurse notices women in a village prefer risky home births due to tradition. What is the best first step?

options.A: Report all pregnant women in the village to the local police
options.B: Provide culturally sensitive education and build trust regarding hospital delivery benefits
options.C: Refuse to treat any woman who has previously given birth at home
options.D: Ignore the practice since culture cannot be influenced by health workers

explanation: Yarn true! Respecting people's culture while gently building trust is the best way to help them see the safety of hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main reason a community clinic keeps a dedicated referral register book?

options.A: To advertise traditional medicine options to local residents
options.B: To calculate the monthly salaries of visiting medical doctors
options.C: To record the personal daily attendance of nursing staff members
options.D: To track outgoing cases, dates, and receiving facilities for auditing

explanation: Brilliant! Logging every referral helps clinics keep a clean record of who was sent out, when, and where they went.

question: Which specific nerve gives you conscious control over your external urethral sphincter?

options.A: Pudendal nerve
options.B: Obturator nerve
options.C: Sciatic nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

explanation: You're mastering neuroanatomy! The pudendal nerve carries the signals that let you voluntarily hold or release urine.

question: What defines direct contact transmission?

options.A: Carrying of pathogens by biting insects like mosquitoes
options.B: Inhalation of tiny dried respiratory droplets floating in the air
options.C: Spread of germs through contaminated drinking water supplies
options.D: Physical transfer of pathogens between an infected person and a susceptible host

explanation: Direct contact requires physical touch or direct exposure to bodily fluids without any intermediary objects or surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which lung issue is most common for a patient stuck on prolonged bed rest in traction?

options.A: Hyperventilation syndrome
options.B: Asthma attack
options.C: Atelectasis
options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

explanation: Well done! Lying flat and breathing shallowly can cause small air sacs in the lungs to collapse (atelectasis). That's why deep breathing exercises and incentive spirometry are so important!

question: Which of these is a key administrative duty for a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Designing new blueprints for hospital buildings
options.B: Serving as the legal defense attorney for the hospital
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for the pharmacy
options.D: Conducting regular performance appraisals for ward staff

explanation: Great job! Doing performance reviews helps managers guide their team members, support their growth, and keep ward standards high.

question: How does the VAPP Act change how society and the law view domestic abuse within homes?

options.A: It turns domestic abuse into a punishable criminal offense.
options.B: It leaves punishment to traditional village elders.
options.C: It requires financial compensation without any legal trial.
options.D: It treats domestic abuse as a private family dispute.

explanation: Well done! Domestic abuse is no longer seen as a mere 'family secret' or private affair—it is a crime with legal consequences.

question: How often should you check a stable newborn's vital signs right after birth?

options.A: Every 30 minutes until stable for two hours
options.B: Every 15 minutes for the first 24 hours
options.C: Only when the baby begins to cry or feed
options.D: Once every hour throughout the entire hospital stay

explanation: Keep a close eye on them! Vitals should be checked every half hour until the baby maintains steady vitals for a solid two hours.

question: How can a tele-nurse help assess a patient's physical status from afar?

options.A: Guessing the vital signs based on the patient's age
options.B: Relying entirely on laboratory tests done once a year
options.C: Guiding the patient or caregiver to perform simple checks at home
options.D: Physically walking to the patient's house for every assessment

explanation: You got it! You can coach the patient or a family member on how to check simple things like pulse rate or swelling at home.

question: Which type of nutrient transport across cell membranes requires the body to use energy (ATP)?

options.A: Facilitated diffusion
options.B: Osmosis
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Well done! Just like carrying a heavy load uphill, active transport needs a little boost of cellular energy (ATP) to push nutrients where they need to go.

question: What are the main jobs of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile and filtering toxins from the blood
options.B: Secreting hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor
options.C: Digesting proteins and absorbing simple sugars
options.D: Absorbing water and compacting indigestible waste

explanation: Well done! The large intestine mainly soaks up remaining water and turns leftover food into solid stool ready for elimination.

question: A client comes to the clinic asking for a reversible method that lasts for several years without her needing to remember it daily. Which option fits best?

options.A: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking with her partner
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken every morning
options.C: An intrauterine device inserted into the uterine cavity
options.D: Male withdrawal practice during intercourse

explanation: Great choice! Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are long-acting and give continuous protection for years without needing daily action from the client.

question: What is the main job of thermoreceptors in the skin?

options.A: Sensing tissue damage caused by sharp objects
options.B: Detecting relative changes in skin temperature
options.C: Regulating core body temperature via sweat production
options.D: Converting mechanical vibration into electrical signals

explanation: You got it! Thermoreceptors fire up when they notice shifts in temperature, rather than just steady warmth or cold.

question: You notice a crying baby's front soft spot looks a bit bulging. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Document the finding as severe hydrocephalus immediately
options.B: Apply firm pressure to flatten the fontanelle back down
options.C: Prepare an immediate referral for suspected increased intracranial pressure
options.D: Soothe the infant, place them upright, and reassess when quiet

explanation: Brilliant! Always calm the baby first so you can get a true, reliable reading instead of a false alarm.

question: A nurse refuses extra training because she believes management never promotes anyone fairly anyway. Which part of Vroom's theory is broken here?

options.A: Expectancy
options.B: Physiological need
options.C: Valence
options.D: Instrumentality

explanation: Instrumentality is your belief that good performance will actually lead to the promised reward. If you feel the system is rigged, that link is broken.

question: Why does Addison's disease make a patient's skin turn a darker, bronze color?

options.A: Elevated levels of hormones that stimulate melanin production
options.B: Chronic dehydration leading to skin darkening
options.C: Increased exposure to sunlight caused by fatigue
options.D: Poor circulation trapping pigment in superficial capillaries

explanation: In Addison's, the brain pumps out extra signals to try and stimulate the adrenals; these hormones accidentally stimulate skin pigment (melanin) too, causing a dark tan look.

question: What is the key difference between a synthetic drug and a semi-synthetic drug?

options.A: Synthetic drugs only come from plant roots, while semi-synthetic drugs come exclusively from mineral rocks.
options.B: Semi-synthetic medications require no clinical trials, whereas fully synthetic medications require extensive testing.
options.C: Synthetic drugs cannot be given orally, whereas semi-synthetic drugs can only be given via intravenous injection.
options.D: Semi-synthetic drugs modify a natural base compound in a lab, while synthetic drugs are built entirely from scratch.

explanation: Think of semi-synthetic drugs as natural molecules upgraded in a lab, while purely synthetic ones are built from scratch using basic chemicals.

question: Why are accurate nursing records about needle counts so important in a court of law?

options.A: They show how fast the surgical team can work
options.B: They prove that standard safety protocols were followed
options.C: They help the hospital calculate patient food bills
options.D: They determine the salary of the operating theatre staff

explanation: You're doing great! Clear charting is your best legal protection, proving you did your job safely and correctly. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: A community health nurse conducts a household survey to count active tuberculosis cases. What type of data is this primarily?

options.A: Hypothetical data
options.B: Quantitative data
options.C: Secondary data
options.D: Qualitative data

explanation: Counting active cases involves numerical measurements, which classifies the information as quantitative data. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary source in nursing research?

options.A: A systematic review article written by an outside professor
options.B: A newspaper editorial commenting on a new health policy
options.C: A textbook chapter summarizing ten different research articles
options.D: An original research report written by the scientists who did the study

explanation: Primary sources are direct, firsthand accounts written straight by the actual researchers who performed the study.

question: Which of these is a rare but very serious complication unique to laparoscopy?

options.A: Gas embolism
options.B: Mild tooth decay
options.C: Simple skin rash
options.D: Dry scalp scaling

explanation: You're doing great! If the gas used to inflate the tummy accidentally gets directly into a blood vessel, it can travel to the heart or lungs, creating a dangerous gas embolism.

question: How does the poliovirus mainly spread from person to person?

options.A: Vector-borne mosquito bites
options.B: Fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct sexual contact
options.D: Aerosol droplet inhalation

explanation: You've got this! The virus usually spreads when someone unknowingly eats or drinks something contaminated with tiny amounts of infected waste matter.

question: What is the characteristic shape of the sigmoid colon?

options.A: A tight circular ring
options.B: A horseshoe curve
options.C: An S-shaped loop
options.D: A straight vertical tube

explanation: Spot on! It's called the sigmoid colon because it bends like the letter 'S' as it leads down to the rectum.

question: Why might a surgeon need to perform a craniectomy (removing a piece of the skull) after severe brain trauma?

options.A: To remove the primary injury site completely
options.B: To permanently cure the patient's concussion
options.C: To relieve dangerous pressure caused by brain swelling
options.D: To clean out surface dirt from a skull fracture

explanation: You got it! Taking off a piece of the skull gives a swollen brain room to expand outward instead of crushing vital areas inside.

question: What happens to the pupils of your eyes when the parasympathetic system is stimulated?

options.A: No change in pupil size
options.B: Uncontrolled twitching
options.C: Pupil dilation
options.D: Pupil constriction

explanation: Parasympathetic signals make the circular muscles in your iris contract, which causes your pupils to constrict (get smaller). Keep going, you've got this!

question: How do governments use healthcare spending as a percentage of GDP?

options.A: To calculate individual patient prescription costs
options.B: To set the daily working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To determine the required passing grade for nursing students
options.D: To measure how much national wealth goes toward medical care

explanation: This ratio shows the proportion of a country's total economic output dedicated to keeping people healthy and running health services.

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling polio vaccines?

options.A: To activate the chemical preservatives inside the glass vial
options.B: To keep the liquid vaccine from freezing solid in storage
options.C: To prevent the heat-sensitive vaccine from losing its potency
options.D: To ensure the vaccine changes color before administration

explanation: Spot on! Polio vaccines are fragile biological products that break down and become useless if exposed to too much heat.

question: What is the difference between data fabrication and data falsification?

options.A: Fabrication applies to nursing, falsification applies to physics
options.B: Fabrication is inventing fake data, while falsification is altering real data
options.C: Fabrication is legal with IRB approval, falsification is never allowed
options.D: Fabrication is stealing text, falsification is stealing money

explanation: You got it! Fabrication means making numbers up from thin air, while falsification means tampering with real results.

question: Why should community nutrition counseling respect local food traditions?

options.A: Families are much more likely to follow advice that fits their culture
options.B: Traditional recipes always contain zero nutritional value
options.C: Cultural habits prevent any form of weight gain
options.D: Nurses are legally forbidden from discussing local foods

explanation: When you work with a family's cultural food habits instead of fighting them, they are way more likely to stick with your healthy changes!

question: How does culture influence a person's health-seeking habits?

options.A: It dictates the exact laboratory values for blood pressure
options.B: It determines the anatomical structure of human organs
options.C: It prevents individuals from ever feeling physical pain
options.D: It shapes how they view, express, and seek treatment for sickness

explanation: Culture guides our beliefs! It teaches us how to talk about pain, who to consult first, and what healing should look like.

question: A patient expresses deep regret over past actions and asks if God can ever forgive them. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Dismiss the worry because everyone makes mistakes
options.B: Tell the patient that nurses only handle physical medications
options.C: Advise the patient to stop thinking about the past
options.D: Acknowledge their concern and offer to connect them with a spiritual care provider

explanation: Spiritual distress is real pain. Acknowledging it and connecting them with a chaplain or spiritual leader gives them the holistic support they need.

question: What is the main medication given alongside other treatments for hydatid disease?

options.A: Albendazole
options.B: Aspirin
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Amoxicillin

explanation: Albendazole is the go-to antiparasitic drug used to weaken or shrink the cysts before or after surgery.

question: Why are secondary complications so dangerous for patients with brain or nerve injuries?

options.A: They can worsen the initial injury and cause further damage
options.B: They disappear without any medical intervention
options.C: They always reverse the effects of the primary disease
options.D: They only affect the peripheral nervous system

explanation: Secondary problems put extra stress on a body that is already struggling, often leading to a much worse outcome than the original injury. You've got this!

question: What is a major safety risk for patients with Pick's disease due to temporal lobe changes?

options.A: Developing sudden and severe bone fractures from walking
options.B: Inability to feel pain when touching hot stove surfaces
options.C: Sudden loss of hearing making them unable to hear fire alarms
options.D: Attempting to eat non-food objects or dangerous substances

explanation: Because of changes in how they experience things orally, these patients might try to chew or swallow harmful objects. Keeping hazardous items out of reach is a crucial nursing priority!

question: Which clinical situation requires the use of intravenous fluid therapy?

options.A: Routine daily multivitamin supplementation at home
options.B: Chronic stable hypertension controlled by diet
options.C: Severe dehydration requiring rapid fluid replacement
options.D: Mild headache treatable with swallowing pills

explanation: When fluids must be restored quickly or the gut cannot absorb them, the intravenous route is the fastest solution. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of involving the PTA when community health nurses visit a school?

options.A: It prevents teachers from participating in health programs
options.B: It helps secure parental consent and reduces fear among families
options.C: It ensures that students do not pay any school fees
options.D: It allows nurses to take over the daily teaching duties

explanation: Parents trust the PTA leadership, so their endorsement makes community health interventions much more acceptable and successful. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which health education approach uses face-to-face counseling and home visits?

options.A: National television campaign
options.B: Mass media approach
options.C: Individual approach
options.D: Large community lecture

explanation: The individual approach gives personalized education through direct one-on-one time, like patient counseling or home visits.

question: How many fundamental questions form the foundation of the Model for Improvement?

options.A: Three
options.B: Five
options.C: Seven
options.D: Ten

explanation: Great job! The framework relies on just three core questions to guide any quality improvement project from start to finish.

question: Which drug is commonly used first when a mother has postpartum hemorrhage from a soft uterus?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Furosemide

explanation: You got it! Oxytocin helps the uterine muscle contract strongly to stop heavy bleeding.

question: Which type of insurance guarantees that you have your own personal lawyer separate from the hospital's legal team?

options.A: Individual malpractice policy
options.B: Universal health coverage
options.C: General workers' compensation
options.D: Group facility indemnity policy

explanation: An individual policy is yours alone. It ensures a lawyer is hired specifically to look out for your personal license and career.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team needed for comprehensive FGM care?

options.A: Patients refuse to speak to nurses unless a doctor is present
options.B: Surgeons are legally required to manage all aspects of nursing care
options.C: Medical insurance only covers care if multiple specialists sign off
options.D: The physical, psychological, and obstetric needs of survivors are complex

explanation: Because FGM affects physical health, childbirth, and mental health all at once, teamwork among different specialists gives the patient the best care possible. You're doing awesome!

question: Someone is caught helping a traditional cutter prepare instruments for FGM. Under the VAPP Act, what is this helper's legal status?

options.A: Guilty of aiding and abetting the offense
options.B: Responsible only if the victim is under five years old
options.C: Exempt from punishment because they did not hold the blade
options.D: Subject only to a verbal warning from community leaders

explanation: Spot on! The law doesn't just punish the person doing the actual cutting; anyone who helps, encourages, or joins in is also guilty of the crime.

question: What should you do FIRST when a portable monitor suddenly lets out a loud, urgent alarm?

options.A: Document a cardiac arrest in the patient chart right away
options.B: Immediately silence the device and walk away to find a doctor
options.C: Turn off the monitor power switch to stop the annoying noise
options.D: Assess the patient's physical condition and check the sensor placement

explanation: Patient first, always! Check the patient and make sure the sensor hasn't just popped off before jumping to conclusions.

question: Why do lab scientists often prefer molecular genetic tests over traditional culture methods for tricky microbes?

options.A: Genetic tests are always performed at the patient bedside by nurses
options.B: Molecular methods eliminate the need for any laboratory safety equipment
options.C: Culture methods cannot tell the difference between bacteria and viruses
options.D: Molecular methods identify organisms directly from genetic material without slow culture growth

explanation: Growing germs in a culture dish can take agonizingly days or weeks. Molecular tests find the DNA directly, giving quick answers when patients need care fast!

question: What should a nurse watch closest right after a patient gets an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Urine output using a bedside commode
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal softness
options.C: Cardiac rhythm and vital signs
options.D: Range of motion in the upper arms

explanation: You've got this! Because the heart muscle was just punctured, tracking heart rhythm and blood pressure helps catch dangerous complications right away.

question: What type of care usually triggers automatic DRF exemptions during an emergency?

options.A: Long-term physical therapy
options.B: Annual medical fitness checkups
options.C: Emergency trauma resuscitation
options.D: Routine elective cosmetic surgery

explanation: When every second counts, emergency trauma care gets fast-tracked so lifesaving supplies are never delayed by paperwork.

question: As a community health nurse on a home visit, what is one of your key duties?

options.A: Prescribing high-risk surgical medications
options.B: Assessing living conditions and providing counseling
options.C: Replacing routine laboratory equipment
options.D: Performing major surgical procedures at home

explanation: You're checking out the environment and chatting with mum about good food, hygiene, and what danger signs to watch out for. Great nursing practice!

question: How can health facilities best fix the problem of staff underreporting due to a fear of blame?

options.A: By firing every nurse who makes a minor documentation error
options.B: By hiding all disease statistics from the government ministry
options.C: By stopping all surveillance activities during busy seasons
options.D: By fostering a supportive, blame-free work culture that values data

explanation: When staff know they won't be unfairly punished for honest mistakes, they are much more open and accurate with their reporting. Spot on!

question: An adverse event is best described as an injury that:

options.A: Results from medical management rather than the illness
options.B: Always results from extreme medical negligence
options.C: Only happens during major surgical procedures
options.D: Stops a patient from ever recovering fully

explanation: Think of an adverse event as any unintended medical injury linked to the care provided, whether it could have been prevented or not.

question: What is the term for a medical error that is so shocking and preventable it should simply never happen?

options.A: Sentinel event
options.B: Never event
options.C: Near miss
options.D: Adverse event

explanation: Exactly! 'Never events' are catastrophic mistakes—like operating on the wrong body part—that strict safety rules are built to completely wipe out.

question: Which of the following is an indirect method to assess medication adherence?

options.A: Checking tissue biopsies for microscopic drug deposits
options.B: Analyzing urine specimens for active chemical traces
options.C: Counting the remaining pills in the medicine bottle
options.D: Measuring exact drug metabolites in a blood sample

explanation: Pill counts, patient interviews, and refill records are indirect ways to check compliance without laboratory drug assays. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which injection is routinely given to every newborn baby to prevent dangerous bleeding?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Iron drops
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Newborns have little tummies that haven't built up clotting factors yet. Giving Vitamin K right after birth protects them against bleeding disorders. Excellent clinical knowledge to carry into the ward!

question: Why are babies and young children extra vulnerable to the risks of self-medication?

options.A: They refuse to swallow any medication unless it is sweet
options.B: Their liver and kidney enzyme systems are still immature
options.C: Their skin absorbs chemical substances much slower than adults
options.D: They have higher blood volume than healthy adults

explanation: Spot on! Children's bodies process drugs differently because their organs aren't fully developed yet to clear toxins easily.

question: Which type of budget takes care of daily running costs like medical supplies and generator fuel?

options.A: Emergency surplus budget
options.B: Capital budget
options.C: Operational budget
options.D: Personal investment budget

explanation: The operational budget keeps the lights on and the supplies stocked for everyday patient care.

question: What is the main goal when a patient is caught early with non-small cell lung cancer?

options.A: Total lung transplantation
options.B: Surgical resection
options.C: Palliative hospice care
options.D: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy

explanation: You're doing great! If the cancer is caught early and hasn't spread, cutting out the tumor surgically gives the best chance for a complete cure.

question: What is another common name for prenatal care?

options.A: Neonatal monitoring
options.B: Postpartum care
options.C: Gynecological screening
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Prenatal care is widely referred to as antenatal care, representing health services provided during the period of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: A patient with terminal cancer is unable to speak but is frowning, restless, and breathing rapidly. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The patient is fully relaxed and ready for sleep
options.B: The patient is recovering normal neurological function
options.C: The patient is having an allergic reaction to food
options.D: The patient is experiencing untreated pain or discomfort

explanation: Non-verbal patients often show pain and distress through behavioral cues like frowning, restlessness, and changes in respiratory rate. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of a descriptive statistic?

options.A: A surgical success prediction model
options.B: The exact biological cause of a virus mutation
options.C: A proven cure rate for a genetic disorder
options.D: Percentage of patients with high blood pressure

explanation: Numbers like percentages, averages, and counts are classic descriptive statistics that simply summarize what is happening in the data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why are recreational play breaks important alongside structured classroom lessons?

options.A: They allow teachers to grade papers without student interruptions
options.B: They provide a necessary mental break to refresh student focus
options.C: They ensure students never feel tired during school hours
options.D: They completely replace the need for physical education curricula

explanation: Brief periods of unstructured play reduce mental fatigue, helping students return to class more attentive and ready to learn. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: Who on the healthcare team is the go-to expert for designing specialized medical nutrition therapy?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The staff ward nurse
options.C: The registered dietitian
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: Dietitians have specialized training to create specific medical nutrition plans for patients with complex health needs.

question: What are the small, yellowish deposits that build up under the retina in dry age-related macular degeneration called?

options.A: Melanin granules
options.B: Drusen
options.C: Aqueous humor
options.D: Crystalline proteins

explanation: Great work! Drusen are tiny fatty deposits that collect under the retina as we age. Finding them is a key sign of dry macular degeneration.

question: What is the very first thing you should do for a baby right after a home birth?

options.A: Transport the newborn immediately to a distant clinic
options.B: Give the baby a full soap bath in warm water
options.C: Dry the infant thoroughly with a clean, warm towel
options.D: Clamp and cut the umbilical cord before drying

explanation: Drying and wrapping the baby fast is key to keeping them warm and preventing cold stress.

question: Which home care instruction is most critical for a patient who just had a liver biopsy?

options.A: Call the clinic or return if you feel severe shoulder or belly pain
options.B: Go for long daily jogs to boost blood circulation
options.C: Scrub the tiny wound hard with soap immediately
options.D: Take aspirin every morning to prevent clots

explanation: You got it! Severe pain can be an early warning sign of internal bleeding or other complications, so patients must report it right away.

question: What is the primary goal of screening pregnant women for home delivery?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any further antenatal visits
options.B: To separate low-risk mothers from those who need hospital care
options.C: To calculate the exact date and hour labor will begin
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing baby clothes

explanation: Screening helps identify who can safely give birth at home and who requires a facility with advanced medical help. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the main job of the trophoblast layer in a developing blastocyst?

options.A: It surrounds the egg to form the protective corona radiata
options.B: It forms the outer layer that assists with implantation and placenta development
options.C: It develops directly into the internal organs of the growing fetus
options.D: It creates the fast block to prevent extra sperm from entering

explanation: You nailed it! The trophoblast acts like a pioneer, helping the embryo burrow into the uterine lining to build a healthy placenta.

question: Why was isolating pure chemical compounds from crude plants a major improvement in medicine?

options.A: It ensured that medicines could only be produced in rich countries.
options.B: It made plants completely unnecessary for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
options.C: It allowed healthcare providers to control dosages and predict effects accurately.
options.D: It completely eliminated all possible side effects of medications.

explanation: Crude plant mixtures vary wildly in strength depending on soil and weather, whereas pure isolated chemicals allow precise and safe dosing. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h4)

question: A community health nurse is teaching a mother how to improve her family's protein intake using affordable local foods. What is the best advice?

options.A: Combine local plant sources like beans and maize to get complete proteins
options.B: Feed the family exclusively imported vitamin pills instead of meals
options.C: Avoid all local staple carbohydrates like yam and cassava completely
options.D: Rely only on expensive red meat imported from overseas

explanation: Pairing local plant foods like beans and maize gives you a complete protein combo without breaking the bank. Brilliant nursing care!

question: A community health nurse finds three new cases of tuberculosis in a neighborhood. What is the best immediate step for managing the human reservoir?

options.A: Spraying chemical disinfectants on local streets and pathways
options.B: Tracing and screening close contacts of the infected individuals
options.C: Ordering all residents in the town to stay indoors for a month
options.D: Vaccinating all stray dogs and cats living near the neighborhood

explanation: Contact tracing lets us find other people who might be carrying the germ without knowing it yet, so they can get checked and treated early.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to treat drinking water?

options.A: Adding appropriate chlorine treatment
options.B: Boiling it thoroughly
options.C: Storing it uncovered in a warm, dusty corner
options.D: Using a certified water filtration system

explanation: Exactly! Leaving clean water uncovered is an open invitation for dust, flies, and germs to sneak right back in and contaminate it.

question: A nurse meets a shy 15-year-old girl from a low-income home who expresses fear of getting pregnant. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Inform her parents right away without discussing it with the teenager first
options.B: Focus the discussion entirely on unrelated physical symptoms like headaches
options.C: Provide non-judgmental counseling, education on contraception, and connect her with youth-friendly resources
options.D: Tell the teenager to stop speaking with boys immediately and send her home

explanation: Empowering teens with practical knowledge and supportive resources is the most effective nursing approach to prevent adverse outcomes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h9)

question: How does keeping girls in school benefit the wider community and economy?

options.A: It guarantees that every family will receive direct cash stipends
options.B: It empowers future workers and boosts family health and financial stability
options.C: It eliminates all local taxes for households with daughters
options.D: It completely stops rural-to-urban migration patterns

explanation: Well reasoned! Educated women earn better incomes, make healthier choices for their children, and help lift their communities economically.

question: In community nursing, how do we best describe a "community"?

options.A: A single hospital ward with patients and staff
options.B: A collection of medical doctors working in one clinic
options.C: Every person living within a country's capital city
options.D: A group of people sharing values, interests, or geography

explanation: Spot on! Think of a community as people connected by bonds, shared spaces, or common goals—not just four hospital walls. You're getting the hang of this!

question: What happens to a Plaster of Paris cast if it gets wet?

options.A: It dries out and becomes twice as hard as before
options.B: It shrinks tightly and cuts off blood circulation
options.C: It changes color from white to bright yellow
options.D: It softens, weakens, and loses its structural shape

explanation: Unlike fiberglass, traditional plaster will break down and lose its strength when exposed to water. Keep it dry!

question: At what age should solid foods be introduced alongside breast milk or formula?

options.A: Twelve months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Nine months

explanation: You got it! By six months, breast milk alone isn't quite enough to match a growing baby's big nutritional demands, so it's time for tasty complementary foods.

question: Why does the body form small bumps called granulomas during a TB infection?

options.A: To help transport oxygen across damaged alveolar membranes
options.B: To produce antibodies that neutralize the bacterial toxins
options.C: To wall off and contain the bacteria within the lungs
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of red blood cells

explanation: Think of granulomas as a smart defensive wall built by your immune system to trap the TB germs so they cannot wander around your lungs.

question: What is the primary goal of home health care?

options.A: To replace traditional long-term nursing home facilities
options.B: To provide permanent 24-hour bedside critical care
options.C: To help patients recover and live independently at home
options.D: To reduce the workload of busy hospital physicians

explanation: Home health services focus on bringing medical and support care to the residence so individuals can manage conditions and recover safely where they live. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of routine family planning services?

options.A: Adolescent reproductive health education
options.B: Infertility management and counseling
options.C: Provision of modern contraceptive methods
options.D: Performing major abdominal surgeries

explanation: You got it! Family planning clinics focus on counseling, birth control, and fertility support—not major operations like removing an appendix.

question: What symptom makes vitamin B12 deficiency different from simple iron deficiency?

options.A: Elevation in total white blood cell counts
options.B: Severe swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Presence of neurological symptoms like numbness
options.D: Rapid drop in liver enzyme production

explanation: B12 protects our nerves! When it's missing, patients can experience tingling or numbness in their hands and feet, which doesn't happen in plain iron deficiency.

question: Which activity must a patient strictly avoid right after having nose or ear surgery?

options.A: Sleeping on their back
options.B: Walking around the room
options.C: Drinking cool water
options.D: Forceful nose blowing

explanation: You've got it! Blowing your nose hard builds up a lot of pressure inside your head, which can pop open stitches, knock out clots, and cause fresh bleeding.

question: If a community health nurse notices that immunization rates remain low despite running a vaccination campaign, what should be done next?

options.A: Investigate the barriers causing the low uptake and adjust the strategy
options.B: Report the village to the police for failing to cooperate
options.C: Pretend the campaign was a success and submit fabricated data reports
options.D: Assume the community does not care about health and stop all programs

explanation: Evaluation is an ongoing feedback loop; when targets are missed, nurses must analyze the root causes and modify their approach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which member of the healthcare team is best at helping a patient relearn everyday tasks like bathing, dressing, and cooking?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Speech pathologist
options.C: Respiratory therapist
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're doing fantastic! Occupational therapists focus on daily 'occupations'—helping patients gain independence with self-care tasks so they can get back to living their lives.

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge that leads to unsafe injection practices in low-resource settings?

options.A: High patient demand for parenteral treatments
options.B: Shortages of single-use sterile injection equipment
options.C: An overabundance of certified auto-disable syringes
options.D: The operation of informal and unregulated drug vendors

explanation: Facilities actually suffer from shortages of safe equipment, not an overabundance! Lack of supplies is a major hurdle.

question: Which structure acts as the body's master biological clock for daily rhythms?

options.A: Adrenal cortex
options.B: Pineal gland
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Suprachiasmatic nucleus

explanation: Found in the hypothalamus, the suprachiasmatic nucleus uses light cues from your eyes to manage your 24-hour body clock.

question: Which health problem commonly happens right after severe flooding?

options.A: Immediate eradication of vector-borne parasites from local water tables
options.B: Outbreaks of waterborne illnesses like cholera and typhoid fever
options.C: A sudden spike in industrial chemical burn injuries across urban factories
options.D: Widespread occupational lung cancer among adult agricultural workers

explanation: When floodwaters mix with drinking sources, bacteria love it. That is why nurses always watch out for waterborne infections like cholera after floods!

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To lower the financial cost of operating public hospitals
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To develop knowledge for nursing practice and improve patient outcomes
options.D: To replace physicians in diagnosing complex medical conditions

explanation: Nursing research focuses on building a scientific base for nursing care so patients receive the safest and most effective interventions. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do vulnerable population groups need special healthcare approaches instead of regular programs?

options.A: Government policy forbids them from visiting general clinics
options.B: They refuse to take any standard orthodox medications
options.C: They face unique barriers like poverty, isolation, and stigma
options.D: Standard programs are too expensive for hospitals to run

explanation: Spot on! Because of hurdles like distance, poverty, or discrimination, standard health programs often fail to reach them without special adjustments.

question: What is the primary way researchers share their completed findings with the professional community?

options.A: Shredding documents to protect hospital secrets
options.B: Publishing articles in peer-reviewed journals
options.C: Telling patients secretly during hospital discharge
options.D: Posting personal opinions on social media apps

explanation: Peer-reviewed journals are the gold standard for distributing verified research to other professionals. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is a common misunderstanding caregivers have about normal vaccine reactions?

options.A: Total absence of any reaction proves the vaccine failed to work
options.B: Crying after an injection means the child has developed an allergy
options.C: Mild fever and swelling mean the child is harmed and should skip future doses
options.D: A slight rash indicates the child is now immune to all known diseases

explanation: You're doing great! Parents sometimes mistake normal, mild immune responses like a low-grade fever for a dangerous sickness and skip the next shots.

question: What is the biggest danger of leaving dysphagia untreated in a patient?

options.A: Chronic skin rashes
options.B: Permanent hearing loss
options.C: Sudden kidney failure
options.D: Aspiration pneumonia

explanation: When food or drink slips down the wrong pipe into the lungs, it brings bacteria right along with it. This is why watching how patients swallow is so crucial!

question: How do most drugs travel from a pregnant mother to her baby?

options.A: Direct swallowing of amniotic fluid
options.B: Filtration through the fetal kidneys
options.C: Active pumping by the umbilical cord
options.D: Simple diffusion across the placenta

explanation: Medicines in the mother's bloodstream mostly cross over the placenta easily through simple diffusion to reach the baby. You've got this!

question: How can cultural beliefs negatively impact a community's health status if ignored by health workers?

options.A: The birth rate might increase without affecting disease transmission
options.B: The local government might run out of financial grants for road construction
options.C: Weather patterns could shift and cause unexpected droughts
options.D: People may avoid formal health facilities and rely on harmful traditional practices

explanation: When health workers ignore cultural beliefs, patients often reject modern treatment in favor of familiar traditions, leading to delayed care and worse health outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is it actually helpful for bedside nurses to understand basic health economics?

options.A: It helps them appreciate the operational challenges of resource allocation and patient flow
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing chronic illnesses in the community
options.C: It allows them to negotiate direct commission fees for prescribing medications
options.D: It removes the need for doctors to write formal treatment orders

explanation: Spot on! Knowing economics helps you understand why management makes certain staffing decisions and how best to manage patient beds on your ward.

question: A hospital unit arranges all high-alert drugs in the exact same alphabetical order in every medication room. What safety design principle is this?

options.A: Complex redundancy
options.B: Punitive discipline
options.C: Manual override
options.D: Standardization

explanation: Exactly! Keeping supplies and medications laid out identically across multiple units prevents confusion and helps nurses find what they need quickly and safely.

question: Why might older clinicians sometimes slow down the acceptance of new nursing practices?

options.A: They control the international accreditation of school curricula
options.B: They automatically receive higher salaries than reform advocates
options.C: They may prefer traditional workflows over new evidence-based guidelines
options.D: They are legally barred from entering modern hospital wards

explanation: Spot on! It's human nature to stick to what you are used to, so older staff can sometimes be hesitant with brand new routines.

question: Which medication group requires careful review before a pacemaker insertion due to bleeding risks?

options.A: Anticoagulants
options.B: Antihistamines
options.C: Antacids
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: Blood thinners increase the risk of bleeding into the surgical pocket where the pacemaker battery is placed. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why does a drop in immunization coverage pose a major danger to a community?

options.A: It leads to severe outbreaks of preventable diseases
options.B: It causes immediate antibiotic resistance in infants
options.C: It increases the cost of treating chronic genetic disorders
options.D: It permanently ruins the cold chain storage equipment

explanation: When too many children miss their shots, community immunity falls, allowing dangerous infections to return and spread rapidly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: What does follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) do in the ovaries?

options.A: It helps immature eggs inside the ovaries grow.
options.B: It causes the muscular wall of the uterus to contract strongly.
options.C: It immediately stops all blood flow to the endometrium.
options.D: It thickens the outer layer of the vaginal walls.

explanation: True to its name, FSH 'stimulates' the little follicles in the ovary so the eggs inside can grow and get ready for action.

question: Which action best demonstrates the nurse's role in interprofessional drug information exchange?

options.A: Consulting with the hospital pharmacist to clarify an ambiguous drug dosage order
options.B: Writing the discharge prescription without consulting the medical team
options.C: Changing a patient's medication dose independently when side effects appear
options.D: Deciding which new drugs the hospital pharmacy committee should purchase

explanation: Working closely with pharmacists ensures safe medication practices through collaborative communication. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a baseline functional assessment before starting rehab?

options.A: To discharge the patient from the hospital immediately
options.B: To prove that the patient cannot recover
options.C: To measure future progress and guide the care plan
options.D: To determine the final cost of medical insurance

explanation: Exactly! The baseline gives us a clear starting line so we can track how much the patient improves over time.

question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: To restrict patient access to common over-the-counter drugs
options.B: To make safe and effective medicines affordable and available
options.C: To eliminate the need for international pharmaceutical trade
options.D: To promote expensive brand-name pharmaceuticals in hospitals

explanation: You got this! The core idea is simple: making sure everyday life-saving medicines remain cheap enough and within reach for everyone who needs them.

question: Why is daily record keeping at local primary health clinics important for disease surveillance?

options.A: It proves to international donors that local nurses are working hard
options.B: It stops patients from visiting traditional healers in the village
options.C: It helps health authorities spot unusual increases above the normal baseline early
options.D: It guarantees an immediate increase in government funding for clinics

explanation: Consistent clinic records provide the baseline data needed to detect outbreaks early through routine surveillance. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h5)

question: Why is the separation of maternal and fetal blood inside the placenta important?

options.A: It prevents an immune reaction and protects against certain infections
options.B: It ensures that fetal blood pressure remains higher than maternal pressure
options.C: It allows blood cells to mix freely to boost the fetal immune system
options.D: It stops the mother from absorbing too much fetal waste

explanation: Keeping maternal and fetal circulations separate prevents the mother's immune system from attacking fetal cells and blocks many harmful pathogens from passing directly over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a rehabilitation hospital?

options.A: Restoring lost function and maximizing independence
options.B: Treating acute infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Stabilizing immediate life-threatening organ failure
options.D: Providing long-term terminal palliative care

explanation: You got this! Rehab hospitals help patients rebuild their strength and everyday skills after major life changes, rather than managing sudden medical emergencies.

question: Which animal is the main reservoir responsible for spreading the Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Stray cats
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Pigs and swine
options.D: Multimammate rats

explanation: You got it! Lassa fever is mainly passed to humans through contact with the urine and droppings of infected multimammate rats.

question: A stroke patient has weak arms on one side, but she can still wash her face if her wash basin is placed close by. What should you do?

options.A: Tell her family to do all her bathing when they visit
options.B: Wait until her full strength returns before she bathes
options.C: Encourage her to wash her upper body while you assist with the rest
options.D: Do everything for her to save her energy

explanation: Wonderful choice! Encouraging whatever independence a patient has left boosts their mood and helps them recover faster.

question: Why shouldn't nurse educators rely on just one single learning theory?

options.A: Students will complain if they only experience one teaching style
options.B: Different nursing skills and learning goals require different theoretical approaches
options.C: Accreditation bodies legally require schools to use all five theories
options.D: Only one theory has ever been scientifically proven to work

explanation: Nursing is diverse! Simple procedures need different teaching approaches than complex clinical reasoning, so mixing theories gives the best results.

question: Why do doctors often prescribe hormonal contraceptives for women with oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: To induce regular withdrawal bleeding and protect the uterine lining
options.B: To permanently stop the natural production of all body hormones
options.C: To permanently cure the underlying genetic defect in the ovaries
options.D: To stimulate the immediate release of multiple eggs every month

explanation: Spot on! Contraceptives help shed the uterine lining on a regular schedule, preventing it from building up too much when natural ovulation isn't happening.

question: Why are chemotherapy drugs considered dangerous for the nurses who handle them?

options.A: They always emit a poisonous gas that fills the entire hospital ward
options.B: They are designed to kill cells and can harm the nurse's cellular health
options.C: They cause immediate fainting if the nurse smells them
options.D: They instantly burn through standard hospital uniforms and skin

explanation: Chemo drugs work by destroying cells. That makes them powerful treatments for patients, but it also means nurses must handle them with extreme care to avoid toxic exposure.

question: Why is having clear rules for DRF exemptions so important for hospital staff?

options.A: It stops staff from showing personal bias when giving out free drugs
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to increase drug prices for wealthy patients
options.C: It ensures that doctors do not have to write any medical prescriptions
options.D: It guarantees that the federal government will pay the hospital bonus funds

explanation: Clear criteria remove guesswork and favoritism, making sure that only genuinely qualified patients receive free medications.

question: Which of these conditions is an example of a functional (rather than structural) birth defect?

options.A: A cleft palate
options.B: Transposition of the great vessels
options.C: An absent lower limb
options.D: Congenital hypothyroidism

explanation: Congenital hypothyroidism messes with hormones and metabolism (how the body works), whereas the other options are physical body parts formed differently.

question: Which complication is most directly linked to sluggish blood flow in the legs of an immobile patient?

options.A: Orthostatic hypotension
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Peripheral neuropathy
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Immobility slows venous return from the lower extremities, which allows blood clots to form more easily in deep veins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: What type of pen ink is recommended for writing in manual health records to ensure longevity?

options.A: Washable water-based ink
options.B: Pencil for easy erasing
options.C: Red ink for all entries
options.D: Permanent black or blue ink

explanation: Permanent ink ensures that records do not fade, smudge with humidity, or get easily altered over time. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h7)

question: How does the hippocampus work when it comes to human memory?

options.A: It acts as the final permanent storage vault for every memory
options.B: It translates what you see into spoken words
options.C: It organizes new memories and helps send them to the cortex
options.D: It deletes sad memories to protect your mental health

explanation: Correct! Think of the hippocampus as a sorting station that processes new memories and helps ship them to the cerebral cortex for permanent storage.

question: Why is a kidney infection (pyelonephritis) so dangerous for a pregnant woman?

options.A: It thickens the amniotic fluid until fetal movement stops completely
options.B: It stops the liver from producing essential blood-clotting proteins
options.C: It can trigger systemic sepsis and stimulate premature uterine contractions
options.D: It automatically causes permanent blindness in the developing fetus

explanation: High fever and severe infection put the whole body under massive stress, which can easily trick the womb into starting early labor.

question: Why do government health systems often partner with non-governmental agencies?

options.A: Communities prefer private doctors over public nurses
options.B: Ministries of health do not care about rural populations
options.C: Hospitals lack enough space to store modern medicines
options.D: Government facilities face funding limits and personnel shortages

explanation: You got it! Because budgets and staff numbers can be tight, government agencies often need extra hands to reach every corner of the country. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: When giving eye drops, where is the safest spot to place the liquid?

options.A: Directly onto the center of the cornea
options.B: Into the lower conjunctival sac
options.C: Onto the upper eyelid surface
options.D: Into the inner corner tear duct

explanation: Dropping the medicine into the lower pocket keeps the delicate cornea safe from scratches while letting the drop spread evenly across the eye.

question: Why must food be digested before your body can absorb it?

options.A: Digestion adds essential vitamins that trigger active transport
options.B: The stomach cannot hold food unless it is first broken down
options.C: Unbroken food particles will immediately cause an immune reaction
options.D: Complex molecules are too large to cross the intestinal mucosal lining

explanation: Think of it like trying to pass a big couch through a tiny doorway—large food molecules simply cannot fit across the intestinal wall until they are chopped down into smaller pieces!

question: Which body problem is a very common cause of sudden confusion or unconsciousness?

options.A: Severe hypoglycemia
options.B: A ruptured cerebral aneurysm
options.C: Bacterial meningitis
options.D: A penetrating skull fracture

explanation: Spot on! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), the brain gets starved of its main energy source and shuts down fast.

question: If an older child or teenager faints right after getting an injection, what is this usually classified as?

options.A: Immunization anxiety-related reaction
options.B: Coincidental infection process
options.C: Product-related systemic reaction
options.D: Vaccine quality defect-related reaction

explanation: Needle fear is real! Fainting right after a shot is typically an anxiety-related reaction, not a bad reaction to the vaccine itself.

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning before discharging a post-abortion care patient?

options.A: Contraceptives cure existing pelvic infections
options.B: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization
options.C: It prevents the onset of menopausal symptoms
options.D: Fertility can return very quickly after a termination

explanation: Brilliant! Ovulation can start as early as two weeks after an abortion, so counseling helps prevent unplanned repeat pregnancies.

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Spraying household furniture with industrial bleach daily
options.B: Keeping all windows tightly closed during visits
options.C: Performing proper and frequent hand hygiene
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every home visit

explanation: Good old handwashing and using alcohol rubs remove germs fast, protecting both you and your patient from cross-contamination.

question: What do we call the ability to recognize a familiar object (like a key or coin) just by touching it with your eyes closed?

options.A: Graphanesthesia
options.B: Extinction
options.C: Stereognosis
options.D: Proprioception

explanation: Stereognosis is your brain's neat trick of 'seeing' with your hands through touch alone.

question: Why do we need special care when doing research with vulnerable groups?

options.A: To prevent exploitation and protect them from harm
options.B: Because they always pay large amounts of money
options.C: To satisfy international tourism guidelines
options.D: So the researcher can finish data collection quickly

explanation: Vulnerable patients need extra protection because they might easily feel pressured to agree to a study. Keeping them safe is our top priority.

question: What is the first crucial step before collecting data in a new community?

options.A: Writing a final report for the federal ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all children under five
options.C: Demolishing illegal structures that block drainage systems
options.D: Community entry and gaining the trust of local leaders

explanation: Without properly introducing the team to local leaders and gaining entry, residents may be uncooperative and data collection will fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why should hospital waste bags be tied up when they are only three-quarters full?

options.A: To ensure the waste weighs exactly the same as household garbage
options.B: To prevent overfilling, tearing, and accidental spills during transit
options.C: To give the cleaning staff enough time to take a lunch break
options.D: To allow the municipal collection agency to charge lower fees

explanation: Exactly! Leaving a bit of space at the top lets you tie the bag securely and stops nasty spills on the way out.

question: Which population group often develops metabolic health risks at much lower BMI thresholds?

options.A: Competitive endurance runners
options.B: Individuals of Asian descent
options.C: Adult males over sixty years old
options.D: Pregnant women in their third trimester

explanation: You nailed it! Research shows that people of Asian descent can face higher cardiovascular and metabolic risks at lower BMI numbers.

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Gradual resistance of body cells to normal insulin
options.C: Temporary hormone changes during pregnancy
options.D: Poor dietary intake of refined carbohydrates

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Brilliant to keep this distinction in mind!

question: If a diet study relies entirely on patients writing down what they ate in a diary, what limitation should you mention?

options.A: Excessive use of expensive laboratory equipment
options.B: Too many blood samples taken from participants
options.C: Potential bias from self-reported data
options.D: Severe physical injuries caused by the diary

explanation: Spot on! People sometimes forget what they ate—or write down what they *wish* they ate. We have to keep that in mind!

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical focus of occupational health nursing?

options.A: Managing pediatric developmental milestones in schools
options.B: Promoting the use of proper personal protective equipment
options.C: Inspecting work areas for ergonomic strain and safety risks
options.D: Identifying workplace hazards like toxic chemicals

explanation: Occupational health deals specifically with worker safety and workplace hazards, not school-aged child development. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h6)

question: What standard p-value do nursing researchers usually look for to prove statistical significance?
explanation: 0.05 is the gold standard in research! It tells us there's a 5% or lower chance our results happened purely by random luck.

question: A nurse checks daily blood glucose numbers sent automatically from a patient's smart glucometer at home. What is this called?

options.A: Electronic health record archiving
options.B: Store-and-forward imaging
options.C: Remote patient monitoring
options.D: Synchronous tele-surgery

explanation: Great job! Remote patient monitoring uses connected home devices to keep an eye on vital signs without the patient needing to visit the clinic.

question: A patient is brought to the clinic after a motorcycle crash, and clear fluid is dripping from one nostril. What serious injury should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Severe allergic reaction to helmet padding
options.B: Fracture of the cribriform plate with CSF leak
options.C: Rupture of the maxillary paranasal sinus
options.D: Inflammation of Kiesselbach's vascular plexus

explanation: Clear fluid coming from the nose after a head impact is a major red flag. It usually means a skull fracture has torn the lining near the brain, letting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak out. Always report this immediately!

question: Why should patients take artemether-lumefantrine tablets with fatty food?

options.A: Fat neutralizes the bitter taste of the crushed tablets
options.B: Fat coats the stomach to completely prevent any nausea
options.C: Fat helps the kidneys excrete the drug much faster
options.D: Fat significantly improves the absorption of the lumefantrine component

explanation: Wonderful! Lumefantrine dissolves best in fat, so a fatty meal helps the body absorb it properly to knock out the malaria.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to source or store eye medications in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: Buying products only from verified, licensed pharmacies
options.B: Keeping drops away from direct sun and heavy heat
options.C: Buying medications from roadside hawkers to save money
options.D: Checking the expiry date before every application

explanation: Never buy drugs from roadside vendors! They often sell fake, expired, or poorly stored medications that can ruin vision or cause dangerous eye infections.

question: How do bacteria usually share drug resistance traits with each other so quickly?

options.A: By shedding their outer cell walls in hostile environments
options.B: Through horizontal gene transfer using plasmids
options.C: By slowing down their normal rate of cell division
options.D: Through direct physical consumption of dead human cells

explanation: Bacteria love sharing! They pass small loops of DNA called plasmids directly to their neighbors, spreading resistance traits across different types of germs like gossip in class. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a core feature of youth-friendly healthcare services?

options.A: Displaying non-judgmental staff attitudes
options.B: Providing affordable or free services
options.C: Demanding parental consent for every minor interaction
options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality

explanation: If a clinic demands parental permission for every little thing, scared teens simply won't come. Youth-friendly care balances guidance with privacy so young people still seek help.

question: Why is it unsafe to use ordinary adhesive tape to fix a frayed electrical cord on a medical device?

options.A: Adhesive residue ruins the texture of the plastic casing
options.B: Tape does not provide safe insulation against electrical shock
options.C: It prevents the biomedical engineers from seeing the color
options.D: It makes the equipment look untidy during hospital rounds

explanation: Quick tape fixes don't have the proper safety protection to stop electrical shocks or short circuits. Always tag it for biomedical engineering instead!

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for causing salpingitis?

options.A: Treponema pallidum and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Klebsiella pneumoniae

explanation: Chlamydia and gonorrhea are the sexually transmitted bacteria behind the vast majority of acute salpingitis cases. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: What core belief serves as the absolute foundation of the primary health care philosophy?

options.A: Advanced hospitals are more important than rural clinics
options.B: Health is a fundamental human right for everyone
options.C: Traditional medicine must be banned from public facilities
options.D: Modern medicine should be funded entirely through private loans

explanation: Primary health care is built on social justice, treating health as a basic right rather than a privilege for the rich. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main reason for using separate cutting boards for raw meat and fresh vegetables?

options.A: Complying with modern kitchen aesthetic trends
options.B: Ensuring that the wooden boards dry out faster
options.C: Preventing cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.D: Keeping the vegetable board from smelling like spices

explanation: Using separate boards stops bacteria from raw meat from transferring to foods that will be eaten raw or lightly cooked. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h5)

question: Why do uterine contractions eventually become weaker during a prolonged, blocked labour?
