options.C: Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
options.D: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)

explanation: PEP is taken promptly after a potential exposure to stop the virus before it takes hold. Stay safe out there!

question: Which specific protein in the intestine makes Oral Rehydration Therapy work so well?

options.A: SGLT1
options.B: Gastric lipase
options.C: Potassium pump
options.D: Insulin receptor

explanation: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose linked transporter type 1) is the hero protein! It links sugar and salt uptake in the small intestine to pull precious water into the body.

question: What is usually the very first step when preparing to study a community?

options.A: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all school children
options.C: Gaining entry and building trust with local community leaders
options.D: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the local clinic

explanation: Before collecting data, nurses must respect local protocols and gain the cooperation of community leaders to ensure participation. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is the immune system called a 'diffuse' system instead of just one single organ?

options.A: It relies entirely on the brain to direct every defensive action
options.B: It only functions when a person is actively sleeping or resting
options.C: It changes its physical structure completely every few days
options.D: It consists of cells, tissues, and organs spread throughout the body

explanation: Unlike the heart which stays in one place, your immune cells are everywhere! They travel through your blood, lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow all at once.

question: What is the main role of the thalamus when processing sensory information?

options.A: Act as a relay station to filter and direct signals to the cortex
options.B: Store long-term memories of painful experiences
options.C: Control the physical movement of the sensory organs
options.D: Convert mechanical waves into electrical nerve impulses

explanation: Think of the thalamus as the ultimate sorting office in the brain. It checks incoming sensory messages and routes them to the right neighborhood in the cortex for you to experience them.

question: Which important nutrient should you encourage in the diet of a patient with heavy periods?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Sodium

explanation: Losing a lot of blood means losing iron, which can lead to tiredness and anemia. Pushing iron-rich foods is a classic nursing intervention!

question: Why is data cleaning an essential step before running statistical tests?

options.A: It eliminates the need to obtain ethical clearance
options.B: It ensures all participants completed the survey
options.C: It catches entry errors and impossible values that distort results
options.D: It automatically converts nominal data into ratio data

explanation: Cleaning data allows researchers to spot typos and unrealistic entries, ensuring the final statistical findings reflect true clinical observations. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is herd immunity so important for infants who are too young for certain vaccines?

options.A: It cures any congenital infections the infant was born with
options.B: It lowers the chance that the infant will encounter the infectious agent
options.C: It passes mature white blood cells directly through breast milk
options.D: It permanently removes all pathogens from the surrounding environment

explanation: You got it! When everyone around the baby is vaccinated, it builds a protective shield that keeps nasty germs far away from vulnerable little ones.

question: As a community health nurse, what is your very first step when starting a referral?

options.A: Calling an ambulance service before assessing the patient
options.B: Asking the patient to pay administrative referral fees
options.C: Writing a discharge summary for the local health board
options.D: Identifying a clinical condition that exceeds the clinic's capacity

explanation: You've got this. The referral process only begins once you realize the patient's medical needs are too advanced for your local clinic to handle alone.

question: What does a delayed capillary refill time usually indicate about the patient?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake during the day
options.B: Poor peripheral blood circulation
options.C: An infection in the heart valves
options.D: High levels of oxygen in the blood

explanation: When blood flow to the extremities is sluggish, it takes longer for color to return to the nail bed after pressing. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why does safe motherhood include mental and social well-being alongside physical health?

options.A: Because total health affects a woman's ability to care for herself and her baby
options.B: Because mental health issues only occur after delivery
options.C: Because physical health cannot be measured during pregnancy
options.D: Because social status is the only cause of maternal mortality

explanation: A holistic view of health recognizes that emotional and social support are just as vital as physical care for a mother and her child. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h1)

question: When would a clinician choose indirect ophthalmoscopy over direct ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: When performing a quick bedside neurological check on a ward
options.B: When examining the far periphery of the entire retina
options.C: When only a small portion of the central optic disc needs viewing
options.D: When the patient cannot tolerate any bright light shining near them

explanation: Indirect ophthalmoscopy provides a much wider, stereoscopic view that allows the examiner to see the far edges of the retina. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which check uses the mid-upper arm size to spot severe weight loss or wasting in children?

options.A: Clinical examination
options.B: Biochemical analysis
options.C: Body measurement (anthropometry)
options.D: Radiological imaging

explanation: Spot on! Anthropometry simply means taking body measurements like height, weight, and arm size to see how well a child is growing.

question: Why do oesophageal varices carry such a high risk of dangerous bleeding?

options.A: The walls of these enlarged veins are thin and fragile
options.B: High blood pressure causes the entire tube to rupture
options.C: Swallowed food particles puncture them easily
options.D: Stomach acid quickly digests the surrounding tissue

explanation: Think of them like over-inflated balloons. Because the blood pressure inside them is so high and their walls are stretched thin, they can tear and bleed very easily.

question: What is the ultimate goal of interpreting research data in nursing?

options.A: To help university professors publish more academic textbooks
options.B: To give hospital managers more paperwork to file away
options.C: To improve patient care and guide evidence-based clinical practice
options.D: To reduce the number of nurses working in hospital wards

explanation: At the end of the day, research data only matters if it helps us make patient care safer and better!

question: Which common side effect should you watch out for in patients taking lots of aluminum-based antacids?

options.A: Rapid hair loss
options.B: Constipation
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Severe diarrhea

explanation: Aluminum has a way of slowing things down in the GI tract, so patients often complain of constipation. Good to keep in mind for nursing care!

question: Who are considered key stakeholders in community mobilisation?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.B: Pharmaceutical company owners only
options.C: Patients admitted to distant urban hospitals
options.D: Only foreign aid workers from abroad

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are influential figures who help guide community opinions and behaviours. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why do inactivated (killed) vaccines often need multiple booster doses?

options.A: The live virus inside them multiplies too quickly
options.B: The killed organisms produce a weaker immune response than live ones
options.C: They do not contain any antigens to trigger B-cells
options.D: They destroy existing memory cells in the bloodstream

explanation: You nailed it! Since the germs are dead and can't multiply, boosters give our immune system a helpful reminder to keep us protected.

question: What is the name of the upper opening into the true pelvis?

options.A: Acetabulum
options.B: Pelvic inlet
options.C: Pelvic outlet
options.D: Greater sciatic notch

explanation: You're doing great! The pelvic inlet is literally the 'entrance' or upper opening where the baby first enters the true pelvis.

question: Why is it so important to quickly isolate a suspected Ebola patient in a clinic?

options.A: It allows the lab to make local drugs
options.B: It prevents the virus from spreading to other patients and healthcare staff
options.C: It eliminates the need to wear protective gowns
options.D: It cures the patient before bleeding starts

explanation: Spot on! Isolating patients cuts off the transmission chain immediately and keeps everyone else in the ward safe.

question: What is the most important home safety change to make in the bathroom after an amputation?

options.A: Replacing all porcelain fixtures with plastic ones
options.B: Removing the bathroom door to improve airflow
options.C: Installing grab bars near the toilet and shower
options.D: Painting the bathroom walls a bright, cheerful color

explanation: Wet bathroom floors plus new mobility challenges spell danger. Grab bars and shower seats keep baths safe and independent!

question: What do we call the top number in a blood pressure reading?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure
options.B: Systolic pressure
options.C: Diastolic pressure
options.D: Pulse pressure

explanation: Spot on! The top number measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart beats. That's your systolic pressure.

question: How do civil service rules and professional nursing acts work together for a public sector nurse?

options.A: Civil service rules completely replace professional nursing laws upon employment
options.B: The nurse must obey both administrative civil service rules and professional health regulations
options.C: The constitution prevents nurses from being held accountable to civil service guidelines
options.D: Professional council regulations only apply to private hospital nursing staff

explanation: As a public sector nurse, you answer to two bosses in a way: your administrative employers (civil service rules) and your profession (the nursing council).

question: A researcher targets prisoners for a risky drug trial just because they are locked up and easy to reach. Which ethical rule is being broken?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Justice
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Spot on! Justice means fair selection, so vulnerable groups aren't unfairly dumped with all the riskiest studies.

question: Which nursing action is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Teaching joint exercises to a stroke survivor
options.B: Providing wound care for a chronic leg ulcer
options.C: Conducting a blood pressure screening at a market
options.D: Administering the routine childhood measles vaccine

explanation: Vaccines prevent healthy people from developing an infection in the first place, making them a primary prevention measure. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: Iron, calcium, and potassium belong to which group of nutrients?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Vitamins
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Minerals

explanation: Correct! These are essential minerals that help keep your bones strong, fluids balanced, and body reactions running smoothly.

question: What is the sympathetic nervous system mainly doing while your bladder is filling up?

options.A: Increasing parasympathetic outflow to the bladder wall
options.B: Contracting the detrusor muscle and relaxing the internal sphincter
options.C: Stimulating the pudendal nerve to open the external sphincter
options.D: Relaxing the detrusor muscle and contracting the internal sphincter

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your 'rest and storage' helper. It relaxes the bladder wall so it can expand and keeps the exit tightly shut so you don't leak!

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.A: To treat infertility using modern assisted reproductive technology
options.B: To cure advanced stages of reproductive tract cancers
options.C: To stop health problems before they start through screening and education
options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept diseases early or stop them entirely using vaccines, screenings, and education. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the 'Hawthorne effect' in a research study?

options.A: The sudden drop in blood pressure caused by new drugs
options.B: Alteration of behavior by subjects who know they are being observed
options.C: A permanent loss of study participants over time
options.D: The financial cost of running a large hospital trial

explanation: Correct! People naturally change how they act when they know someone is watching them, which can sometimes trick our research findings.

question: Why can tubal damage from salpingitis lead to an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Damaged cilia cannot properly propel the fertilized egg to the uterus
options.B: Hormone levels drop so low that the uterus rejects the embryo
options.C: The ovaries release eggs too rapidly for the uterus to prepare
options.D: The uterine lining becomes too thick for any implantation

explanation: The tiny hair-like cilia inside the tube get damaged by the infection, so they can't sweep the fertilized egg down to the uterus as they normally would.

question: Why is dietary counselling considered a collaborative process rather than just giving a printed diet sheet?

options.A: Printed diet sheets are illegal for nurses to distribute in a hospital
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.C: It involves an interactive dialogue and assesses personal eating habits
options.D: Patients are required to cook meals for the entire nursing staff

explanation: Collaboration means working together through conversation to understand the patient's real lifestyle rather than just handing over generic paperwork. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h1)

question: Which action represents effective nursing advocacy in food policy?

options.A: Personally financing the national agricultural subsidy budget
options.B: Sharing clinical data with policymakers to support nutritional programs
options.C: Refusing to care for patients who eat unhealthy processed foods
options.D: Replacing all government food inspectors with hospital nurses

explanation: Nurses use their clinical insights to influence decision-makers and support programs that improve community health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: Why do advocacy networks train healthcare workers on the law around abortion?

options.A: To replace traditional medical school exams with legal bar examinations
options.B: To help staff distinguish between unlawful practices and legal life-saving post-abortion care
options.C: To encourage nurses to perform illegal procedures in private clinics
options.D: To ensure hospitals can sue patients who experience medical complications

explanation: Well done! Clear legal training ensures nurses don't panic and refuse emergency post-abortion care out of confusion or fear.

question: What is the main goal of having a "just culture" in a hospital?

options.A: Allowing senior doctors to break hospital rules without consequences
options.B: Ensuring that every single staff member receives the exact same salary
options.C: Punishing every nurse immediately when a minor paperwork error happens
options.D: Encouraging staff to report mistakes openly without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: Spot on! When nurses and staff feel safe speaking up about errors, the whole hospital becomes safer for everyone.

question: Which sign tells you a newborn baby is working too hard to breathe and has respiratory distress?

options.A: Sternal retractions
options.B: Acrocyanosis of hands
options.C: Coupled heart sounds
options.D: Active limb movement

explanation: When the skin pulls in around the chest bones (sternal retractions), it means the baby is struggling to pull air into their lungs. That's a classic warning sign!

question: How can you tell over time if a patient's diet therapy is working successfully?

options.A: Weight trends and laboratory values
options.B: The brand of cutlery used for meals
options.C: The exact time the hospital kitchen opens
options.D: The color of the hospital room walls

explanation: Checking changes in body weight and lab results gives you clear, undeniable proof of how well the therapeutic diet is working.
